description: Synthetic 90-day incident register for the order-management platform. Symptoms, timestamps, business impact and workarounds only — no stated root cause. See docs/private-issue-manifest.yaml (QA-private) for the private incident-to-trigger mapping. All organisations, users and figures are synthetic.

incidents.business_impact: Order cancellations and fulfilment approvals both stalled for ~40 orders during the evening batch window; on-call paged.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Database session logs show two concurrent transactions each waiting on a row lock held by the other; both transactions eventually aborted with a lock-wait error.
incidents.workaround: On-call manually re-ran the two stuck orders during a quiet period; no code change made.

incidents.business_impact: One customer's shipment was recorded twice in the fulfilment timeline; support had to manually correct the duplicate shipping charge.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Two identical 'shipment created' audit entries with different timestamps ~90s apart for the same order; broker dashboard shows one redelivery in that window.
incidents.workaround: Support de-duplicated the customer-facing record manually.

incidents.business_impact: Fulfilment routing kept using a retired carrier for ~2 hours after an administrator updated the routing configuration.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Configuration audit shows the change was saved; the service's own request logs show it continued applying the old carrier until it was restarted.
incidents.workaround: Ops restarted the service to pick up the change.

incidents.business_impact: Fulfilment requests for a large batch of orders queued for over 15 minutes during a known slow period for the shipping provider; SLA breach recorded for ~30 orders.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Worker pool metrics show active workers pegged at maximum with a growing queue for the full slow-provider window; no individual worker crashed.
incidents.workaround: None — the queue eventually drained once the shipping provider recovered.

incidents.business_impact: Nightly reprocessing job for a large order batch ran progressively slower over the quarter and was terminated by the platform's memory limit twice this month.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Process memory graph climbs steadily and near-linearly with batch progress rather than staying flat; job restarts from the beginning after being killed.
incidents.workaround: Ops split the batch into two manual runs for this cycle.

incidents.business_impact: A single slow shipping-provider response during a promotional spike produced a disproportionate spike in provider call volume, briefly triggering the provider's own rate limiting.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Dependency call count for the affected time window is far higher than the request count that should have generated them.
incidents.workaround: None — provider rate limiting recovered on its own within minutes.

incidents.business_impact: A fulfilment behaviour difference was observed between the staging and pre-production environments after what was believed to be an identical deployment.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Deployment manifests for the two environments differ only in that one configuration key is present in one profile and absent in the other.
incidents.workaround: None recorded; flagged for engineering review.

incidents.business_impact: An order was simultaneously approved by one agent and cancelled by another; the customer received a fulfilled-item notification for a cancelled order.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Status history for the order shows both transitions recorded within the same second, with no rejection of either.
incidents.workaround: Support manually reconciled the customer's order and issued a refund.

incidents.business_impact: A fulfilment event was generated for an order but never appeared in the downstream shipping-notification system after a deployment restart during processing.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Order status shows fulfilled; no corresponding outbound event or shipping-notification record exists for that order.
incidents.workaround: Support manually triggered the shipping notification once identified.

incidents.business_impact: A customer-facing request that was cancelled by the user (page navigated away) continued consuming backend resources for its full duration.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Request trace shows the client disconnected at ~2s but the corresponding backend dependency call and its logs continue for several more seconds.
incidents.workaround: None — self-resolved when the call finished.

incidents.business_impact: A single struggling tenant's repeated dependency failures were followed by unrelated tenants' fulfilment requests also failing for the same period.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Dependency error-rate dashboard shows all tenants failing simultaneously even though only one tenant's requests were the ones actually hitting the failure condition.
incidents.workaround: Ops manually paged the on-call engineer for the affected dependency; no isolation change made.

incidents.business_impact: An emergency bulk status correction performed by support left three orders in a state with no audit trail, complicating a later customer dispute.
incidents.observed_symptoms: Order status field shows the corrected value; the order's audit history has no entry for the correction.
incidents.workaround: Support recorded the change manually in a separate spreadsheet.
